explanation: Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521. Juan Sebastián Elcano brought the last ship, the Victoria, home to Spain in 1522 with 18 men.

claims.text: Magellan did not complete the first voyage around the world: he was killed in the Philippines in 1521, before it ended.
Juan Sebastián Elcano brought the Victoria, the expedition's last ship, back to Spain in 1522.
The Victoria returned to Spain with 18 men aboard.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Britannica's Cano biography says only 18 Europeans had survived the voyage. Other Britannica entries count it differently: one says the ship arrived with a crew of four Indians and only 17 survivors of the 239 Europeans who set out, and another says the survivors included only 17 Europeans and a small number of Moluccans, apart from Cano.

claimResults.note: The count differs across Britannica entries (17 or 18 Europeans, plus a few Moluccans aboard), so '18 men aboard' cannot be confirmed as written.

issues.note: c3 (explanation 'home to Spain in 1522 with 18 men'): sources count 18 European survivors including Elcano, or 17 without him, and a few Moluccans were also aboard. Say 'with 18 of the roughly 240 men who set out'. While there, 'the last ship' could become 'the only ship to complete the voyage', since the Trinidad was still afloat in September 1522.

evidence.restatement: Magellan was killed at Mactan in April 1521 and did not finish the circumnavigation.
